messages:
zoe: Quick note from nightly audit: found several DB snapshot objects under gs://redwood-legacy/snapshots/2017-2020 without our x-encrypt-meta header and no kmsKeyName present.

matt: Can you paste a path and the `gsutil ls -L` output snippet?

zoe: example: snapshots/2018-06/db-prod-20180612.sql.gz -> metadata shows Content-Type + CRC32C only, no encryption headers.

natalie: Timeline suggests pre-CMEK rollout. Which SA did the writes?

zoe: Insert logs point to `backup-uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in 2017-2019. Also one entry from `partner-uploader@vendor.com`.

encops-bot: ALERT: missing_encryption_header detected for 6 objects in redwood-legacy/snapshots. Recommend: audit-insert-events, access-log-scan, test-rewrite.

sre-oncall: Treat as compliance gap. First: scan access logs for any GETs to these keys between 2017-2021. If public reads -> escalate.

matt: Cloud Logging query to run: `resource.type="gcs_bucket" resource.labels.bucket_name="redwood-legacy" protoPayload.methodName="storage.objects.get" protoPayload.request.@type:"storage.objects.get" timestamp>="2017-01-01T00:00:00Z" AND timestamp<"2021-01-01T00:00:00Z"` 

natalie: Also search for SetIamPolicy events granting write to the uploader SA during that window. If infra automation granted broad perms by mistake, we need RBAC rollbacks.

zoe: I ran access log grep -> no public GETs. Reads only from internal SAs and `partner-uploader@vendor.com`.

matt: Remediation plan: 1) add temporary IAM deny for legacy uploader SA (block writes), 2) test `gsutil rewrite -k` on a small set to add kmsKeyName and verify restore, 3) create an escrow manifest mapping original object -> insert event id + upload principal.

natalie: Note rewrite cost + KMS audit trail. Use Storage API rewrite jobs with rate limiting and track kmsKeyRing operations. Record grant IDs.

encops-bot: REMINDER: ephemeral KMS grants for vendor restores must have TTL and be logged. Store grant IDs in escrow manifest.

sre-oncall: Legal, tagging you now as a heads-up. If we confirm plaintext + external reads, we need comms. Otherwise this is internal compliance remediation.

legal: Acknowledge. Prepare a short customer-safe template; we won't send unless security flags a customer impact.

zoe: Test rewrite succeeded on 2 objects, metadata shows `kmsKeyName` and restore to staging DB worked. No errors.

matt: I'll open ENCRYPT-OPS ticket and set priority P2, include Cloud Logging queries, affected keys, and rewrite commands. Also add a CI check to block any new IAAC merges that grant storage.write without `encryption_review=true`.

natalie: Good. I'll add a nightly scanner to flag any objects missing x-encrypt-meta or kmsKeyName and post to the private dashboard.

sre-oncall: If we find any evidence of external reads, escalate to #incidents immediately. Otherwise close as compliance remediation after re-encrypt and RBAC hardening. :lock:
